Whether it’s building robots, participating in speech and debate tournaments, performing in a music group, or playing intramural sports at lunch, the options are endless. By getting involved, students enhance their leadership skills, collaborate with others who share their interests and learn to balance their responsibilities.

All students are encouraged to dive in right from the start. For those with a passion for science, the robotics team offers a chance to design and program vehicles. Artists and performers can take the stage at the International Showcase or our Night of Acoustics, while aspiring poets are invited to share their work at Café Mots. There are also plenty of opportunities for students interested in joining Student Council, engaging in service projects, or participating in intramural sports.
Activity Clubs

3-D Printing Club

Ever wanted to take an idea from your head and turn it into something real you can actually hold? Welcome to the 3D Printing Club — the place to get hands-on time with design software and 3D printers. We’ll teach you everything step-by-step so you can start bringing your own 3D models to life. Join us and see what you can create! No experience necessary. All are welcome!

AI/ML

Learn the workings of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, and help members participate in competitions.

ASL Club

ASL Club is a club wants students to learn about ASL, deaf culture, and being an advocate for people who are deaf. Students don't have to know any ASL to be in the club and attend club meetings. The point is to learn about the Deaf community and learn signs. It's to highlight deaf experiences, events, and even modern day activities that are happening constantly in the deaf community. 

Audio/Visual Club

A/V Club’s responsibilities are to set up and run the liturgies, rallies, and other activities such as the night of acoustics, or dance showcase. We run the sound systems, the light systems, and the presentations or projections.

Aviation & Transportation Club

Learn about the physics, history, and technology behind flight. Starting this year, we're also covering rail and ships. For each mode of transportation, we'll cover their past, present, and future. In addition to meetings on campus, we'll also be taking field trips to museums, airports, and rail depots. 

Baking Club

Baking Club members engage in baking themed activities through watch parties, decorating events, baking contests, and monthly at-home theme baking challenges.

Book Club

Come join Book Club for a fun, inviting space to discuss what we're reading and connect with people who share our love of books. We don't have required reading, but we recommend books across genres and create literary crafts together.

 

Bring Change To Mind

Bring Change to Mind is a National Organization, created to bring awareness and conversation to mental health and reduce stigma in high school communities. 

Build and Design Club

Learning build and design through lego building, gingerbread house contests, and point-perspective workshops.

Calligraphy Club 

The Calligraphy Club is a creative space for students to explore the art of beautiful writing and lettering. 

Car Club

Social club for people who love all things car related. 

 

Chess Club

We provide the opportunity to play and learn more about chess.

Cooking Club

Cooking Club is a group of students who get together 8 times a year after school, learn a recipe from our amazing hospitality staff, cook the recipe and then eat it.  Come join the fun!

Crochet Club

The Crochet Club meets after school and gives students and educators a space to share our passion for crocheting a variety of items from plush toys to blankets. Everyone is welcome regardless of experience level. If you are brand new to crocheting, we will help you get started and encourage you along the way!

Economics Club

For students who want to learn about Economics while playing a variety of games.

Environmental Club

Our club is committed to expanding our understanding of environmental issues. We work to educate our St Francis community and raise our school's standard of sustainability through hands-on activities. Our biggest event is Earth Week. 

Fellowship Of Holy Cross Athletes

Come share your faith journey with other Saint Francis athletes in a collaboration setting.  The group meets once a month for donuts, juice and fellowship.  

Film Club

Film Club is a casual group of students who are interested in the art of filmmaking.  We meet to watch a film as a group, and then have a discussion afterwards.

FMSA

(Future Medical Students Association)

Future Medical Students Association (FMSA) is a club committed to helping students explore the various medical fields in anticipation of medical school. We bring in local health care professionals to educate our club members and host at least one on-campus blood drive per year in partnership with Red Cross. 

Girls Who Code

Girls Who Code strives to increase the representation of women, transgender, and non-binary individuals in technology and to break down the gender barriers that exist in society and the industry. Our goal is to create safe, inclusive spaces and provide opportunities for people of all genders to explore and engage with various Computer Science topics!

Guitar Club 

Social club that invites all musicians of any level to jam on Fridays after school.

Ignite

(Youth Group)

IGNITE is our school's faith-based youth group, run by a core team of students and our Co-Moderators. Founded as a Catholic/Christian space to openly share faith, this group is open to all students of any background to find a space to find community and fellowship. A typical night has free dinner, games, music, a personal sharing, and small groups. We also host on-site Day Retreats such as ENCOUNTER and PATHWAYS. IGNITE is a space where you can be real and belong.

Injury Prevention Club

The Injury Prevention Club promotes safety and helps people learn how to prevent common injuries. IPC members learn about proper exercise techniques, stretching, nutrition, and the importance of specific daily habits. The club also focuses on the mental challenges of being injured, and provides a support space throughout the recovery process.

Quantum Computing Club

Quantum Computing Club is a space for curious students to discover the future of computing. Through projects, discussions, and teamwork, members build a strong foundation in quantum concepts while having fun learning together.

Quiz Bowl 

Quizbowl is a fast paced, buzzer-based game in which players answer questions across various categories. For example, the questions could be from literature, history, science, pop culture, music, and many others. Teams of up to four students compete against other regional teams to qualify for the national tournament that occurs in May in Atlanta. Over the past two years, Saint Francis has achieved deep playoff runs, securing a highest of 21st place nationally at the tournament in 2025. Overall, quizbowl is a great opportunity to have a lot of fun, explore new areas, and build an amazing community together! 

Robotics

Lancer Robotics is the FIRST Robotics Competition team at Saint Francis High School in Mountain View, CA. We pride ourselves in cultivating an engaging environment where students of all classes are provided the opportunity to collaborate with each other alongside experienced mentors with careers in STEM. When we're not engineering our competition robot, Lancer Robotics runs off-season workshops, provides community support through local outreach with our neighboring St. Simon schools, and fosters a strong team dynamic by hosting inter-team events like our annual Minibots competition!

Science Bowl

Club geared towards spreading healthy competitive appreciation towards STEM

Science Olympiad

Science Olympiad is a national STEM competition to challenge students across a wide variety of subjects. Members choose which events they want to compete in, and collaborate in groups to either study for their subject, or build their submission. Competitions go throughout the year and do require competing members to travel around the Bay Area, possibly farther. 

Service Club

Our mission is to unite the school community through meaningful service, fostering compassion, collaboration, and a commitment to making lasting impact in our community and beyond. By hosting monthly service events, we aim to inspire every student to take action and develop leadership skills by serving others.

Sports Medicine Club

The sports medicine club provides students with opportunities to learn about different professions, skills, equipment, and more that exist in the sports medicine world. Meetings will be directed by the students and led by the moderator, so bring all of your medical interests and we can explore them. Meetings can include fun anatomy games, taping instructions, emergency care scenarios, and more. If you're interested in anything sports medicine (e.g Doctor, Physical Therapist, Athletic Trainer, etc) you should check it out!

Stock Market Club

If you are interested in learning about investing tools and financial decisions, the Stock Market club is a competition based club.  We spent our time competing in three national events over the course of the school year - The Wharton Investment Competition (Fall), The Federal Reserve Podcast Competition (Winter/Spring) and the National Economics Challenge (Spring).

Surf Club

The Surf Club shares their love of surfing with the Lancer family, and helps create a community where beginning and experienced surfers can encourage each other.

Society of Women Engineers Next

Explore engineering, build connections, and discover new possibilities in STEM! Through monthly engineering meetings, guest speakers, networking opportunities with engineers, hands-on experiences, and our annual spring conference, we create opportunities for girls to learn about different engineering pathways and connect with professionals and peers. Our goal is to build a supportive community where girls can share experiences, make connections, and grow their confidence in STEM.

Theater Tech

The Technical Theatre club is devoted to bringing the Saint Francis theatre productions to life through Set Design, Lighting Design, Sound Design, and Stage Management. Our club is a great opportunity to build skills in fabrication, painting, leadership, costume design, fly operation, and much more. Tech meets Monday through Thursday from 3:00 - 4:30 with people dropping in whenever they can. We also have Run Crew, a more exclusive tech opportunity, where students have the chance to run productions and be an active member in the rehearsal process.

Ukulele

The ukulele club is one of our performance groups at Saint Francis. We preform at school events like Night of Acoustics in the fall, International showcase, and Christmas in the Quad during Winter. We teach our members how to play ukulele and preform. We also offer singing positions in our club.

An intramural club that meets mostly at lunch for some frisbee fun. All levels welcome to learn how to throw, play the game, and spend time with friends.

Affinity Groups

Asian Student Association (ASA)

Saint Francis High School Asian Student Association (ASA) will be a place where everyone is welcome, especially those of Asian heritage who want to learn more about their identity as an Asian American high school student. It is important that students have opportunities to connect with their roots, and that they have a place to discuss their experience growing up as Asian Americans. Learning about our cultures and heritages is vital to our experience as students developing our hearts and minds to serve the world. We exist so that students can build connections and have access to spaces where they can share, celebrate, and learn more about diverse Asian cultures, traditions, and global events.  Additionally, we provide opportunities for Asian students to process, debrief, and strategize when issues may arise within our school, local communities, and beyond.  

Black Student Union (BSU)
 

Filipino American Student Union (FASU)

Welcome to FASU! We are the Affinity Group for those Lancers who claim Filipino heritage and/or who want to learn more about and elevate Filipino heritage, traditions, and community on campus. We are active and energetic---and ready to welcome you to be part of our FASU Barkada!

Hindu Student Association (HSA)

The purpose of these associations is to promote and celebrate the various aspects of South Asian and Hindu culture through events and other social activities. 

Intersectional Feminist Student Association (IFSA)

The Intersectional Feminist Student Association (IFSA) is a student-led affinity group dedicated to promoting gender equality, inclusivity, and social justice. Through educational events, service projects, and community-building activities , IFSA explores how gender intersects with race, culture, sexuality, socioeconomic status, and other identities. Our goal is to create a supportive space where students can learn about and contribute to helping relevant social justice issues.

Jewish Student Association (JSA)

An affinity group dedicated to exploring Jewish idenity, culture and celebrating Jewish holidays.

Latiné  Student Union (LSU)

The Latiné Student Union (LSU) is a space to celebrate where we come from, learn about the diverse cultures and experiences within our community, and build meaningful connections. It is also a place to learn, grow, ask questions, and challenge ourselves to become better members of our community and the world around us. Here, you’ll find a familia of students and educators on campus who share a connection to the Latiné community and are here to welcome, encourage, and support you.

Whether you are looking for comunidad, want to learn more about your culture and others, or simply want a place where you feel welcomed and supported, there is a place for you in LSU. ¡Bienvenidos!

 

Lusafóno Student Association (LuSA)

Our Affinity Group welcomes students with heritage Portuguese speaking countries and students who are interested in learning more about the Portuguese language and culture (among the various countries where the language is spoken).

Middle Eastern Student Union (MESU)

MESU is a place for students of Middle Eastern heritage and those interested in middle eastern heritage to learn about, celebrate, and share their culture. We are devoted to exploring the diverse cultures and histories of the Middle East while fostering a deeper understanding of Middle Eastern identity.

Muslim Student Association (MSA)

An affinity group where students of the muslim faith or those interest in the muslim faith can explore Muslim identity, culture and celebrate Muslim holidays.

Pride Student Union (PSU)

Pride Student Union is an Affinity group for members and allies of the LGBTQIA+ community at Saint Francis High School. 

South Asian Student Association (SASA)

The purpose of these associations is to promote and celebrate the various aspects of South Asian and Hindu culture through events and other social activities. 

Tagata Pasifika (TP)

We are an affinity group on campus made up of mainly students of South Pacific descent and all who want to join.  We celebrate and share our culture with our communities through dance, song and different events on campus.  All are welcome!

 
Honor Societies

CSF

(California Scholarship Federation – T/A’S, Tutoring Club)

The California Scholarship Federation, Inc. is a nonprofit organization whose mission is to recognize and encourage academic achievement and community service among middle and high school students in California. There are approximately 1500 chapters in middle school and high schools throughout the state, and each chapter is comprised of students members who meet eligibility requirements. Each chapter is led by a staff adviser.
 

NHS

(National Honor Society)

Founded in 1921, the National Honor Society sponsors chapters across the United States and throughout the world. Here at Saint Francis, our chapter recognizes junior and senior students who have maintained exceptional academic records while making significant contributions to their school and local communities. Applicants who exhibit all four of NHS's key pillars--scholarship, service, leadership, and character--are selected for National Honor Society membership. These students play a major role in representing Saint Francis High School through their extracurricular involvement and as Lancer Ambassadors.

 

 

WLHS

(World Language Honor Society)
